justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements (R-01 to R-04) are covered: Patient & Scheduling Component, Kafka Stream Processors (resource clash checks), EMR Component with pgaudit/AWS S3 Object Lock, and Billing Component integrating with Payment Gateway / Insurance Clearinghouse.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-second P95 EMR load is supported by Redis edge caching, PgBouncer connection pooling, Kafka asynchronous processing, and tenant-aware priority routing in API Gateway.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability requirement R-08 is directly addressed by the FHIR Interoperability Component implementing HL7 FHIR APIs and SMART-on-FHIR scopes to exchange data with External Labs & Imaging Systems.
justifications.usability: Web Application (SPA) serves all defined user personas (Doctors, Nurses, Receptionists, Billing Staff, Admins, Patients) via the Clinical Workspace Component, though patients and staff share a single SPA without explicit distinct UI separation.
justifications.reliability: Patroni + etcd automated failover and Kafka KRaft provide strong fault tolerance. However, PostgreSQL is configured as Active-Passive, which partially conflicts with the strict active-active requirement for 99.99% across hybrid regions.
justifications.security: MFA, IdP integration, RBAC/ABAC Policy Enforcement Filter, AES-256 at rest, TDE, TLS 1.3, Vault secrets management, and WORM-compliant AWS S3 Object Lock with KMS envelope encryption comprehensively enforce HIPAA and GDPR compliance.
justifications.maintainability: Components have distinct responsibilities and communicate via Kafka, gRPC, and REST. However, Core Services are grouped into a single container before component-level decomposition, slightly reducing deployment independence.
justifications.portability: The architecture supports hybrid deployment (on-prem-k8s and cloud) using containerized components (NestJS, Kong, Redis, Kafka), though storage tightly relies on AWS S3 Object Lock and AWS KMS.

PERF-01.justification: Redis caching and PgBouncer connection pooling minimize database contention, enabling sub-second P95 load times for 500 concurrent clinicians accessing EMR screens.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio in Redis for active patient records
PgBouncer pool sizing under concurrent round peaks
tradeoffs: Aggressive caching reduces database load but risks serving slightly stale non-critical records

PERF-02.justification: Apache Kafka buffers the 10,000 FHIR results asynchronously, allowing background ingestion without contending with Redis-backed read traffic on the EMR screen.
sensitivity_points: Kafka partition count and consumer group ingestion throughput
Decoupled asynchronous processing between ingestion and EMR querying
tradeoffs: Asynchronous ingestion guarantees query performance at the cost of slight eventual consistency delays

AVAIL-01.justification: The model specifies active-passive PostgreSQL and Patroni failover but lacks multi-region hybrid replication mechanisms or WAN-resilient consensus between on-premises and eu-central-1.
sensitivity_points: Cross-site replication latency between on-premises and AWS eu-central-1
Split-brain avoidance in Patroni cluster across hybrid boundary
tradeoffs: Active-passive hybrid failover avoids multi-primary conflicts but risks high RTO and data loss

AVAIL-02.justification: Patroni with etcd orchestrates database node failover under 30 seconds, while Kafka with transactional outbox and acks=all prevents claim loss or duplication.
sensitivity_points: Patroni leader election timeout and heartbeat frequency
Transactional outbox deduplication keys on insurance claim retries
tradeoffs: Strict acks=all and transactional outbox guarantee zero loss but increase claim submission latency

MOD-01.justification: Claim processing is isolated inside the Billing Component and external clearinghouse interface, ensuring changes are fully contained without impacting the EMR Component.
sensitivity_points: Decoupled event interface between EMR and Billing components
Abstraction level of external insurance clearinghouse adapter
tradeoffs: Isolating billing via asynchronous messaging adds schema maintenance overhead across services

MOD-02.justification: Modifications are strictly limited to the Clinical Workspace component, Patient & Scheduling component, and PostgreSQL engine; pgaudit automatically captures the new field.
sensitivity_points: PostgreSQL schema migration procedures for audited demographics
Automatic schema-level audit tracking via pgaudit extension
tradeoffs: Automated database-level auditing simplifies code changes but increases WAL storage volume

SEC-01.justification: Mandatory MFA is enforced via external IdP and authentication plugins, while Fluentbit streams audit logs; however, real-time alert dispatch relies on external SIEM systems.
sensitivity_points: MFA enforcement policies configured at the Identity Provider
Latency of Fluentbit audit log shipping to security tooling
tradeoffs: Delegating MFA and alerting to external IdP/SIEM enhances security but reduces local observability

SEC-02.justification: Kong ABAC filters and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security enforce access rules, pgaudit logs 100% of read actions, and AWS S3 Object Lock enforces 10-year WORM immutability.
sensitivity_points: Coverage of read-access capture in pgaudit and API filters
WORM compliance mode configuration on S3 Object Lock
tradeoffs: Logging 100% of EMR read operations provides strict compliance but incurs high storage overhead
